--- title: "Session 1: Architecture and kernels" subtitle: "What problem is SPICE solving?" author: "SPICE Book Club · LASP" format: revealjs: theme: [default, custom.scss] slide-number: true preview-links: auto embed-resources: true footer: "SPICE Book Club · Session 1: Architecture and kernels" jupyter: python3 execute: echo: false warning: false --- ## One row of science data {.smaller} An IUVS spectrum from MAVEN, time-tagged by the spacecraft clock. To turn it into science, someone has to answer: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - **When** was it taken, in UTC? - **Where** was MAVEN? - **Which way** was it pointing? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - **What** did the slit see: limb, disk, sky? - **What** was the solar zenith angle there? - **How far** was the light from the target? ::: :::: . . . ::: {.callout} None of these answers is in the science packet. They are **ancillary data**, and each one comes from a different team. ::: ::: notes Start from a measurement everyone in the data systems group has handled. The point: the science file is only useful once it is joined with geometry, and that geometry is somebody else's product. ::: ## Who knows what | Question | Who knows | Cadence | SPICE kernel | |---|---|---|---| | UTC ↔ uniform time | IERS (leap seconds) | rarely | **LSK** | | Clock count ↔ time | mission ops, time correlation | weeks | **SCLK** | | Where is the spacecraft? | navigation (JPL NAV for MAVEN) | days | **SPK** | | Where are the planets? | JPL Solar System Dynamics | years | **SPK** | | Which way is it pointing? | attitude telemetry (spacecraft ops) | daily | **CK** | | How are instruments mounted? | spacecraft builder, instrument team | rarely | **FK**, **IK** | | Shape and spin of the target | IAU, science teams | rarely | **PCK**, **DSK** | ::: {.small .muted} Different owners, different update rates, different sizes, different formats. SPICE's whole design follows from this table. ::: ::: notes Ask the room who on the team has touched each of these, even indirectly. Most will say "time_convert" or "some geometry library" without knowing which kernels sat behind it. ::: ## SPICE's design answer ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 9 %%| fig-height: 4 flowchart LR NAV[Navigation] --> SPK[(SPK)] OPS[Spacecraft ops] --> CK[(CK)] TC[Time correlation] --> SCLK[(SCLK)] INST[Instrument team] --> IK[(FK / IK)] IERS[IERS / IAU] --> LSK[(LSK / PCK)] SPK & CK & SCLK & IK & LSK --> POOL{{"kernel pool
(in your process)"}} POOL --> API["spkpos, sincpt,
scs2e, ..."] API --> YOU[Your code] ``` ::: {.small} Each kind of ancillary data lives in **its own file type**, produced and versioned by whoever owns it. The **toolkit** combines them only at query time. ::: ## Why one answer needs 6–10 files "Where did the IUVS boresight hit Mars at this clock tick, and was it lit?" | Step | Kernel | |---|---| | clock tick → ET | **SCLK** + **LSK** | | MAVEN relative to Mars | **SPK** (MAVEN) + **SPK** (planets) | | spacecraft attitude | **CK** (indexed by SCLK) | | boresight in spacecraft frame | **FK** + **IK** | | Mars shape and orientation | **PCK** (or **DSK**) | ::: {.small .muted} Miss any one and the call fails, loudly. That is a feature: SPICE errors name the missing piece. ::: ## A developer's model ::: {.callout} Kernels are a **read-only, file-backed store** keyed by *(object ID, reference frame, time)*. Each API call is a query against everything loaded. ::: ```python import spiceypy as sp sp.furnsh("session01.tm") # load a list of kernels et = sp.str2et("2026-11-19T12:00:00") # query 1: time (LSK) pos, lt = sp.spkpos("MOON", et, "J2000", # query 2: state (SPK) "NONE", "EARTH") ``` No file names appear in the queries. The **kernel pool** decides which file answers. ## The kernel pool is global state :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **What that means** - One pool per process; every function sees it. - `kclear()` empties it for everyone. - Data loaded **later** win when two kernels cover the same thing. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Why developers care** - Load once, at startup, in one place. - CSPICE is **not thread-safe**: one SPICE caller per process, or a lock. - Log what you loaded (`ktotal` / `kdata`); it *is* your provenance. ::: :::: ::: notes This is the slide most relevant to the data systems group. Long-running services, Dask workers and multiprocessing pools all trip over the global pool. Keep the deeper discussion for the discussion block. ::: ## Two kinds of files | | Text kernels | Binary kernels | |---|---|---| | Types | LSK, SCLK, PCK (text), FK, IK, meta-kernel | SPK, CK, PCK (binary), DSK | | Format | `KEY = value` assignments in `\begindata` blocks | DAF/DAS arrays with a comment area | | Size | kilobytes | megabytes to gigabytes | | Edited by | people, in an editor | programs (`mkspk`, `msopck`, `spkw*`) | | Why | constants humans review and diff | dense time series searched fast | ::: {.small .muted} Text kernels can be read and diffed like code. Binary kernels can't: inspect them with toolkit utilities (`brief`, `ckbrief`, `commnt`) or API calls, never a text editor. ::: ## Inside a text kernel ```{.text} KPL/LSK ← file type ID on line 1 Anything outside a data block is a comment. \begindata DELTET/DELTA_T_A = 32.184 DELTET/DELTA_AT = ( 10, @1972-JAN-1 11, @1972-JUL-1 ... 37, @2017-JAN-1 ) \begintext ``` ::: {#00093b82 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=2} Loaded right now from `naif0012.tls`: **28 entries** in `DELTET/DELTA_AT`, read back with `gdpool`. ::: ::: ## Names are a layer over integers ::: {#ca52b93f .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=3} | Name | NAIF ID | |---|---| | SOLAR SYSTEM BARYCENTER | 0 | | SUN | 10 | | EARTH BARYCENTER | 3 | | EARTH | 399 | | MOON | 301 | | MARS BARYCENTER | 4 | | MARS | 499 | | PHOBOS | 401 | | MAVEN | -202 | ::: ::: ::: {.small} Patterns: barycenters 1–9 · Sun 10 · planets *P*99 · moons *P*01–98 · spacecraft negative · instruments −*SSS*xxx · ground stations 399xxx. Mission kernels add names (e.g. `MAVEN_IUVS`). ::: ::: notes The table is computed live with bodn2c: these mappings are built into the toolkit. Ask: why both 4 and 499 for Mars? Answer next session in SPK land: the planetary SPK gives barycenters; the planet-to-barycenter offset is a separate file. ::: ## Meta-kernels: the list *is* the provenance ```{.text} KPL/MK \begindata PATH_VALUES = ( '../kernels' ) PATH_SYMBOLS = ( 'KERNELS' ) KERNELS_TO_LOAD = ( '$KERNELS/naif0012.tls' '$KERNELS/pck00011.tpc' '$KERNELS/de440s.bsp' ) \begintext ``` - One `furnsh` loads them all, **in this order**: later files have priority. - Relative paths resolve against the **working directory**, not the `.tm` file. - Version the meta-kernel with your code; it records exactly which data you used. ## Read before you trust :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Comments** Who made the file, from what, valid when, known problems. - text kernels: outside `\begindata` - binary kernels: comment area (`commnt`, `dafec`) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Coverage** What the file actually contains. - `spkobj` / `spkcov` for SPK - `ckobj` / `ckcov` for CK - `brief`, `ckbrief` on the command line ::: :::: ::: {.callout} Most "SPICE is broken" reports are a kernel that doesn't cover the time asked for, or the wrong version loaded. Check both first. ::: ## Reading guide for this session | NAIF tutorial | Read for | |---|---| | 03 Overview | the "why" behind today's slides | | 05 Conventions (slides 4, 7–9), 06 NAIF IDs | text vs. binary kernels, file extensions, synonyms; NAIF IDs | | 08 Intro to toolkit, 14 API headers | how to read a function's documentation | | 12 Kernels, 13 Comments | kernel types, meta-kernels, comment areas | | 36 WebGeocalc (optional) | a no-code sandbox for the same queries | ::: {.small .muted} Numbering follows NAIF's current tutorials page. 04 Concepts is read in pieces over Sessions 2–6. Skim 01, 07 and 11 for installation only; in Python, `pip install spiceypy` replaces them. ::: ## Before next session **Homework:** notebook `01_kernels_and_ids` — install check, generic kernels, a hand-written meta-kernel, NAIF IDs, Earth–Moon distance, comments and coverage, MAVEN's instrument IDs. **Reading for Session 2:** tutorial 04 slides 4–13 (time concepts), then 15 (time) and 16 (LSK and SCLK). **Discussion now** - Which kernel types does your current project touch, even indirectly? - Why integer IDs internally? What breaks if two kernels disagree on a name–ID mapping? - What are the risks of the global kernel pool in a long-running service or a multi-threaded pipeline?
